findings.claim: The enum formatter's preprocessor condition is inverted. On modern targets, including .NET 8, the generated EnumFormatter has no ExcludeFromCodeCoverage attribute, while NETSTANDARD2_0 and NETFRAMEWORK are the only targets where the attribute is emitted. This misses enum formatters in the requested coverage and risks using the attribute on precisely the legacy targets for which every other template suppresses it.

receipt_plan.detail: Generate a formatter for an enum referenced by a MessagePackObject using normal .NET 8 preprocessor symbols and inspect the active attributes on the generated enum formatter class. EnumFormatter_IsExcludedFromCodeCoverage_OnModernTargets demonstrates that ExcludeFromCodeCoverage is absent.

findings.claim: Applying ExcludeFromCodeCoverage unconditionally to the generated partial resolver causes CS0579 when the consumer has already applied the same attribute to their partial resolver declaration. Attributes from partial declarations are combined, and ExcludeFromCodeCoverageAttribute does not allow multiples, so existing user workarounds become compile errors.

receipt_plan.detail: Compile a [GeneratedMessagePackResolver] partial class that is also annotated with [ExcludeFromCodeCoverage]. ResolverWithUserSuppliedCoverageAttributeStillCompiles expects no generated-code compilation diagnostics and fails on head with the duplicate-attribute error.
